title: Describe the tool
kicker: World 5 · Have AI Build the Tool · Level 1

job.text:
You've been writing the ask. Now the AI builds real tools you keep.

Up to now the AI's outputs were recorded so a puzzle could never flake. From here it runs live: you describe the tool in your own words, the AI writes it, and a safe runner runs it on real data. The wait is the model thinking, not you failing.

You need a tool that gives total sales for any month from this data — not just this month, every month, without re-asking. In your own words you would type the ask; here you build it from the checklist and commit a success check before you see the output.

moves.label: Ask for the tool, not the answer

text.plain: Don't compute it yourself. Write me a tool that gives the total, don't just tell me a number.
text.tech: Don't compute it inline. Write a function/query that returns the total; don't emit a literal.

moves.label: Say the shape of the tool

text.plain: It takes a month and gives back one dollar total: add up the amount for every row in that month.
text.tech: Input: a month. Output: one numeric total. Rule: SUM(amount) over rows whose date is in that month.

text.plain: Build it so I can run it for any month next time, not just March.
text.tech: Parameterize the month; don't hard-code March.

text.plain: Run it on my data and give me the number it produces.
text.tech: Execute it on the seeded data and report the value it outputs.

text.plain: Please be very careful and double-check your math.
text.tech: Please be very careful and double-check your math.

text.plain: You are an expert data analyst.
text.tech: You are an expert data analyst.

subChoiceGroup: Commit your success check before you see the output (you can't change it after):

subChoices.label: the total equals what the data actually sums to for that month

rules.claim: Tool output for March: 48,210.60 (matches your committed check).
rules.feedback: The tool does the math, and it's reusable. You described it, the AI built it, the runner ran it, and it matches the data exactly — for any month you pass it.
rules.lesson: Describe the tool well and the AI builds something you keep.

output.source: a reusable tool the runner executed on your data

rules.claim: No value to check against — 'about right' can't be run.
rules.feedback: That check can't run. "About right" has no number to compare to, so a wrong answer never fails it. Commit the exact total instead.
rules.lesson: A check needs a value, not a vibe.

output.source: a check with nothing to compare to

rules.claim: Tool output for March: 48,210.60 (hard-coded to March).
rules.feedback: Right once, useless next month. It built a March-only tool. Say "for any month" so you keep it.
rules.lesson: A one-off answer isn't a tool.

rules.claim: Tool output for March: 61,044.25 (summed the wrong column).
rules.feedback: The tool runs but computes the wrong thing. You didn't say what goes in, what comes out, or the rule — so it summed the wrong column. A tool is only as right as the spec you gave it.
rules.lesson: A build is only as good as its spec.

output.source: a vague build with no spec

rules.feedback: That's the guesser again. You asked for the answer, so it predicted one by eyeballing rows. Ask for the tool that produces it.
rules.lesson: A number without a tool is a guess, even live.

hints.nudge: What does the tool take in, and what single number should it give back?
hints.gap: Think of it as input = a month, output = the total. Now say the rule in one line, and say you'll want it again next month.
hints.moves: Add Ask for the tool, not the answer, Say the shape of the tool, Make it reusable, and Run it on my data. Commit the exact check, not "about right".

whatYouDoDifferently.naive: "What were March sales?" → an eyeballed guess.
whatYouDoDifferently.rewrite: "build me a reusable tool: input a month, output the total, sum amount for that month, run it" → an exact total you can rerun for any month.

template.plain: Don't compute this. Build me a reusable tool: it takes [input], returns [one output], by [the one rule]. Run it on my data and give me the result. I'll want to run it again next month.
template.tech: Don't inline this. Write a parameterized function/query: input [param], output [one value], rule [the aggregation]. Execute it on my data and report the result; I'll re-run it with other inputs.

notes: ChatGPT: upload the data; it writes and runs the code, and you can save the code.
Copilot in Excel: ask for a formula that takes the month from a cell, so you change one cell next month.
A chat AI that can't run code: ask for the formula or query and run it yourself; keep it for reuse. Never accept "I checked, it's about right."
